title: Dynamic Cohort-Weighted Eval Index and Canary Scoring Pipeline
creator: Asha Nair
description: Problem: Current regression alerts are noisy and operate on aggregate pass-rate deltas, which hides regressions that affect specific cohorts (e.g., low-context prompts, long-output customers, code-generation). Proposal: build a Dynamic Cohort-Weighted Eval Index (DCWI) and integrate it into a canary scoring pipeline that runs for every config or model change. DCWI combines cohort-specific judgment (LLM-as-judge ensembles calibrated per-cohort) with a meta-weighting layer that adapts based on user traffic and historical sensitivity. Goals: 1) surface regressions that matter to customers earlier; 2) reduce false positives from label noise or rubric drift; 3) provide a single scalar index for quick ops triage plus cohort breakouts for debugging.
approach: Define stable cohorts: traffic-based (top 20 customers), prompt-shape (short/long/instructional), use-case tags (assistants, summarization, coding). Start with 8 initial cohorts and expand via automated clustering.
For each cohort, maintain a small holdout set of curated prompts and a rotating synthetic adversarial set. Holdouts are versioned and seeded per-release.

LLM-as-judge ensemble: run 3 judge models (different families and temperatures) per example; aggregate via majority + confidence scoring. Calibrate ensemble outputs per-cohort using isotonic regression on labeled validation sets.

Meta-weighting: initial weights proportional to cohort traffic and historical business impact (manual override). Implement dynamic adjustment: if a cohort shows high variance or recent sensitivity to config changes, increase its weight automatically.

Canary pipeline: when new model/config is deployed to a canary shard, compute DCWI delta vs baseline; trigger alert if index drops beyond absolute and relative thresholds and if at least one cohort shows >x sigma change.
Expose index and cohort breakdown in Console: time series, heatmap of rubric shifts, per-rubric contribution to index change, and example-level diffs with judge outputs.
Calibration refresh: schedule weekly recalibration using newly labeled data and monthly manual rubric reviews with Design and Research to detect rubric drift.
Guardrails: fuse signal with production telemetry (error rate, latency, user abandonment) to reduce false alarms; require human review for auto-rollbacks.
acceptance_criteria: DCWI computed for every canary run and surfaced in Console canary dashboard
Alerts fire on DCWI regressions with actionable cohort-level context and example diffs
False positive rate of top-1 alerts reduced by >=30% vs baseline aggregate pass-rate alerts in A/B test
Calibration job successfully updates per-cohort isotonic maps and stores versioned artifacts
Playbook created: triage steps, runbook links to PRs and rollback process
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (2 weeks): implement cohort selection, baseline DCWI computation offline, prototype LLM-as-judge ensemble on historical changes (ENG-4120)
Phase 2 (3 weeks): integrate DCWI into canary pipeline for non-critical shards, build Console dashboard prototypes (DES-213, ENG-4481)
Phase 3 (2 weeks): A/B test alerts against existing system, tune thresholds and dynamic weighting heuristics
Phase 4: enable for all canaries and add auto-notifications to SRE/owner rotation; schedule monthly rubric reviews
risks_and_mitigation: Label noise in small cohorts -> mitigate with ensemble judges + confidence thresholds and periodic human re-labels
Overfitting weights to short-term traffic spikes -> smooth weight updates and retain manual caps
Cost of running judges on many examples -> limit to curated holdouts and sampled production traffic; use cheaper judge variants where acceptable
Rubric drift leading to silent calibration failures -> telemetry alerts when calibration maps change dramatically; require guardrail approvals
